 Ian Jeremiah Patrick Sat, 14 November 2026 at 11:00 pm UTC 4 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Billkin Putthipong Assaratanakul may be familiar to Malaysians from the 2024 film ‘How to Make Millions Before Grandma Dies'. — Picture via Instagram/bbillkin KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — From swarming shopping mall concourses to packed concert halls, Malaysian youth culture is experiencing a full-fledged Thai Wave, as Bangkok's screen actors, pop vocalists, and luxury fashion darlings turn Kuala Lumpur into an essential regional tour stop.
 Throughout 2026, an unprecedented procession of Thai celebrities has touched down in the capital, consistently drawing thousands of enthusiastic fans to retail epicentres like Mid Valley Megamall, Sunway Pyramid, and Pavilion Kuala Lumpur.
 Powered by mainstream video streaming platforms and borderless social media communities, contemporary Thai entertainment has matured from a niche online subculture into an economic and pop-culture juggernaut across Southeast Asia.
 Sirilak “Lingling” Kwong even “Most Beautiful Woman Alive 2026” by Netizens Choice Magazine. — Picture via Instagram/linglingkwong Sirilak "Lingling" Kwong even "Most Beautiful Woman Alive 2026" by Netizens Choice Magazine. — Picture via Instagram/linglingkwong
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Leading the charge is Sirilak "Lingling" Kwong, whose performance as Dr Fahlada in the 2024 drama The Secret of Us ignited an ardent regional following. The Hong Kong-born multilingual star, crowned the "Most Beautiful Woman Alive 2026" by Netizens Choice Magazine, parlayed her television success into massive commercial appeal, visiting Malaysia twice this year to headline major brand activations at Mid Valley Megamall in January and Sunway Pyramid in August.
 Win Metawin has moved from drama roles to building a strong presence in the fashion industry. — Picture via Instagram/winmetawin Win Metawin has moved from drama roles to building a strong presence in the fashion industry. — Picture via Instagram/winmetawin
 Equally prominent in the luxury fashion and television circuit is Win Metawin, who vaulted to global prominence through F4 Thailand: Boys Over Flowers and Enigma Black Stage. Serving as Italian luxury fashion house Prada's first Thai global brand ambassador, Win brought his immense star power to Malaysian shores for his maiden solo fan gathering, Just You & Win, drawing crowds to Zepp Kuala Lumpur in May.
 Phuwin Tangsakyuen has gained recognition through acting and music, with his track Truth in the Eyes surpassing 15.7 million streams on Spotify and attracting attention from Malaysian listeners. — Picture via Instagram/phuwintang Phuwin Tangsakyuen has gained recognition through acting and music, with his track Truth in the Eyes surpassing 15.7 million streams on Spotify and attracting attention from Malaysian listeners. — Picture via Instagram/phuwintang
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Win was joined in popularity by fellow GMMTV multihyphenate Phuwin Tangsakyuen, whose acclaimed acting in Fish Upon the Sky and Never Let Me Go is matched by a burgeoning music career under Riser Music, where his single Truth in the Eyes crossed 15.7 million Spotify streams ahead of his Sunway Pyramid appearances.
 That crossover between high fashion and youth fandom was on full display at Pavilion Kuala Lumpur in April, when actresses Tu Tontawan Tantivejakul and Milk Pansa Vosbein triggered deafening cheers at the opening of Calvin Klein's boutique. Having shared the screen in F4 Thailand and upcoming historical production Scarlet Heart Thailand, Tu has built an enviable acting portfolio through celebrated cinema like Gohan, while Milk has become a pioneering face for the girls' love genre following her leading role in 2024's 23.5 and her breakthrough turn in Bad Buddy.
 Billkin Putthipong Assaratanakul may be familiar to Malaysians from the 2024 film ‘How to Make Millions Before Grandma Dies'. — Picture via Instagram/bbillkin Billkin Putthipong Assaratanakul may be familiar to Malaysians from the 2024 film 'How to Make Millions Before Grandma Dies'. — Picture via Instagram/bbillkin
 The cultural footprint has expanded into regional cinema through Billkin Putthipong Assaratanakul, whose moving performance in the 2024 box-office smash How to Make Millions Before Grandma Dies resonated profoundly across generations of Malaysian cinemagoers. Alongside a chart-topping discography highlighted by his ballad Skyline,
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Billkin joined established screen actress Baifern Pimchanok Luevisadpaibul at the Idea Live Arena in August for the Weibo Cultural Communication Night. Baifern, renowned for her dramatic range across romantic comedies and psychological series like Thicha, has mirrored this cross-border success as an ambassador for premium skincare and lifestyle brands.
 Aphisit Usadee, better known as Ninja, is a member of Thai boyband SuperThai, which is growing in popularity in Thailand and Malaysia.— Picture courtesy of Key Billions Aphisit Usadee, better known as Ninja, is a member of Thai boyband SuperThai, which is growing in popularity in Thailand and Malaysia.— Picture courtesy of Key Billions
 The regional momentum has also fostered direct creative ties. T-pop boyband member Ninja (Aphisit Usadee) ventured into Malaysian cinema by playing Dao in local feature film Tiket Sehala, performing the Thai soundtrack title Fire Burning at its Sunway Pyramid premiere in July.
 Kao Supassara first rose to fame in Thailand through the popular teen drama ‘Hormones’ and made her international film debut this year as the lead star of the Malaysian co-production Kong Tao. — Picture by Choo Choy May Kao Supassara first rose to fame in Thailand through the popular teen drama 'Hormones' and made her international film debut this year as the lead star of the Malaysian co-production Kong Tao. — Picture by Choo Choy May
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Similarly, Hormones star Kao Supassara Thanachat headlined the bilateral film co-production Kong Tao in March, while teen idol Perth Tanapon Sukumpantanasan and actor-musician Archen Aydin, popularly known as Joong, staged high-demand solo fan events at Mid Valley and JioSpace, drawing over 1,500 devotees to Petaling Jaya.
 The rising appetite for Thai entertainment across Malaysia signals an evolving cultural landscape among urban audiences. Bolstered by compelling screenwriting, fluid multi-genre talent, and accessible fan engagement, Thai artists have evolved from screen curiosities into beloved household names, ensuring that Malaysia's embrace of the Thai Wave will only deepen.
